document_metadata.title: 1、EXT. PUBLIC ELEMENTARY SCHOOL - DAY
document_metadata.summary: Mordechai, a timid Hasidic boy, stands before a crucifix at a school with anti-Hanukkah graffiti, clutching his lunchbox as he prepares to enter.

entities.name: Mordechai confronts antisemitic graffiti at school entrance
entities.description: Mordechai, a Hasidic boy, arrives at St. Peter, Paul, and Mary Public Elementary School and stands before a wall defaced with the antisemitic graffiti 'HANUKKAH IS HOMOS,' visibly nervous but resolute as he prepares to enter.

document_metadata.title: 36、INT. MALL OF AMERICA - DAY
document_metadata.summary: Harriet Tubbelman ushers Hammer and Esther into a hidden passage as the door closes behind them, escaping the angry children in the mall.

entities.name: Tony announces Santa's impending departure
entities.description: Tony calls for everyone's attention and informs the children that Santa will have to leave in fifteen minutes, prompting vocal disappointment from the kids.

entities.name: Children express disappointment over Santa's early departure
entities.description: After Tony's announcement, the children react with audible disappointment, boos, and protests of disapproval.

entities.name: Tony threatens children with poorly assembled Christmas presents
entities.description: Tony warns the children that if they continue to complain, they will receive low-quality Christmas presents, such as Barbies with heads on backwards or remote control cars without batteries.

entities.name: Tony allows Esther and Hammer to bypass the line
entities.description: After Esther flirts with Tony and fabricates a story about their son getting ahead in line, Tony relents and lets them pass through the velvet ropes to see Santa.

entities.description: Esther touches Tony's bicep, smiles flirtatiously, and uses a fabricated story about their son to manipulate Tony into letting them cut the line.

entities.name: Hammer and Esther move to the front of the line
entities.description: Ignoring the queue, Hammer and Esther make their way toward the front, drawing objection from Tony but ultimately succeeding in bypassing the line.

entities.name: Santa praises Jimmy for his answer and dismisses him
entities.description: Santa commends Jimmy for being a good boy and tells him to leave after their interaction, reinforcing the false narrative about Jewish rituals.

entities.description: Santa's assistants, Bambi and Tawni, lead Jimmy away from Santa's lap and return by bringing Esther and Hammer into the area behind the curtain.

entities.description: The Hammer warns Santa that he will not be harmed if he remains silent and cooperates with the request to leave immediately.

entities.description: Santa responds to the threat by questioning Hammer's familiarity with him and reminding him of his own status and importance.

entities.name: Hammer reveals his identity by removing his hat and shirt
entities.description: In response to Santa's defiance, Hammer dramatically exposes himself by taking off his clothing, prompting Santa to recognize him.

entities.name: Santa expresses shock at Hammer's survival
entities.description: After recognizing Hammer, Santa reacts with surprise, exclaiming that he believed the Hebrew Hammer to be dead.

entities.name: Hammer draws a gun and points it at Santa
entities.description: The Hammer pulls out a firearm and aims it directly at Santa, escalating the confrontation and asserting dominance.

entities.name: Santa appeals to past friendship and offers peace
entities.description: Santa attempts to de-escalate the situation by addressing Hammer as Mordechai, acknowledging past friendship, and admitting fault in appropriating Hanukkah.

entities.name: Santa signals Bambi and Tawni to seduce Hammer as a peace offering

entities.description: After Tony draws back the curtain, the gathered children are exposed to the armed standoff, causing fear and hushed whispers among them.

entities.description: MC Hammer steps forward from the crowd and emotionally begs The Hammer to refrain from harming Santa, momentarily breaking the tension with an awkward self-aware expression.

entities.description: Santa announces to the children that The Hebrew Hammer plans to cancel Christmas, a statement that is not previously coordinated and which surprises both The Hammer and Esther.

entities.description: Upon hearing Santa declare that The Hebrew Hammer will cancel Christmas, both The Hammer and Esther react with visible surprise and silently communicate their concern.

entities.description: Santa attempts to de-escalate the situation by telling the children that he and The Hebrew Hammer are having a calm, adult discussion, prompting The Hammer to play along.

entities.description: Bambi, speaking with a thick Southern accent, declares her fondness for Jewish men, citing their sensitivity and intellect, which provokes jealousy in Esther.

entities.name: The Hammer resists Bambi's sexual allure due to cultural preference
entities.description: Despite being momentarily drawn to Bambi's appearance, The Hammer rejects her advances by stating he prefers women 'like his matzah—unleavened,' affirming his cultural and personal boundaries.
